source.title: Stitched ViTs are Flexible Vision Backbones
source.authors: Zi-Zheng Pan; Jing Liu; Haoyu He; Jian-Fei Cai; Bo-Han Zhuang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including the appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study stitches pretrained ViT model segments using learned activation-space transformations and reports downstream task performance. This is a conceptual test of whether representations can be connected through stitching, rather than a direct measure of representational similarity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-stitching results on downstream tasks, which bear on V4. References to prior model-stitching work are not counted as results. Most figure curves provide no exact values in the text; rows for them record figure-only values. The reported FLOPs distributions are used to set sampling and are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: SN-Netv2 uses model stitching as an engineering tool to build flexible ViT backbones. Its stitching layers start from a least-squares solution, but the anchors and stitching layers are then jointly fine-tuned end to end on each downstream task. Every reported number is the method's own task score against anchors or against SN-Netv1 after that joint training. None measures how much is lost when one fixed model's representations are mapped onto another's. So these results do not test V4 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. The authors present SN-Netv2 as a flexible, training-efficient ViT backbone for dense prediction. It adds two-way stitching, resource-constrained sampling and LoRA stitching layers, and achieves better Pareto frontiers than SN-Netv1 and competitive performance with anchors. They also note a remaining gap to the small anchor on COCO detection.
record.recipe_differences: Uses model stitching with learned activation transformations, but studies downstream-task performance and improves the training framework with two-way stitching, resource-constrained sampling, and low-rank adaptation; it does not directly calculate representation similarity.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with stitching method and training components; the paper reports low-FLOPs gaps for some stitching configurations and improved curves with ROS and LoRA SL. Dataset/task and anchor pair also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D (Fig. 13–14) gives ImageNet-1K accuracy of DeiT3 stitches with only least-squares-initialized 1×1 stitching layers, before training; it is shown in figures only. Accuracy varies widely by stitch position and direction: Slow-to-Fast is better at low FLOPs, Fast-to-Slow at high FLOPs. Appendix E attributes early-block stitching ease to general low-level features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a model family sharing pretraining, untrained linear (least-squares) stitching between ViTs of different widths preserves much task performance, with loss depending on stitch position and direction.

record.problems: The reported outcomes are downstream task scores, not direct measures of representational similarity or mapping loss. Several plotted results have no exact values in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's additional SN-Netv1, SN-Netv1+TWS, and SN-Netv1+TWS+ROS values at 61G–363G were not extracted; they are component-ablation points rather than independent tests of cross-model representation mapping. Figure 17's other COCO-2017 metrics and the ImageNet-1K, COCO-Stuff-10K, and ADE20K curve points are not individually extracted because exact plotted values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: No alignment measured across scale or capability.
No fixed-model mapping loss reported. Stitches are jointly fine-tuned with the anchors; least-squares-initialization accuracy appears only in figures.
No variation of similarity metric or inputs.
No analysis of causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: This is an engineering paper (T4). Stitching is the tool, and the anchors are fully fine-tuned jointly with the stitching layers. The scores therefore reflect co-adapted networks, not the interchangeability of fixed representations, and no version is tested. The record's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels should be dropped. Only the Appendix D initialization results come close to a mapping test, and they are figure-only, within one model family (DeiT3).

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of representational alignment as model scale or capability increases.
No paired image-caption or cross-modal representation alignment test.
No comparison of independently seeded networks for shared features or subspaces.
Tests stitched ViT segments on downstream vision tasks; does not directly quantify representation similarity, test linear maps separately, relative representations, or unpaired mappings.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Does not vary similarity metrics, neighborhood settings, or input distributions to measure convergence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain representational alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ADE20K and COCO-Stuff-10K stitching results at anchor FLOPs
reader_labels.reason: Stitched systems achieve anchor-like or better downstream scores in these settings (r1–r4, r16, r28). This supports useful stitching on these tasks, not a direct claim about representational distance.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ADE20K small-anchor setting without the complete SN-Netv2 method
reader_labels.reason: The SN-Netv1 and TWS-only stitched results remain below the DeiT3-S anchor at 34G (r13–r15), and the paper reports a detection performance gap between the SN-Netv2 stitch and the small anchor (r12 gives the reported comparison, which is favorable to the stitch). The evidence is task- and method-dependent rather than a direct representation-map test.
